The nearby network terminal is dark; Vark fills out a paper incident form beside a stained coffee cup, spare bandages and worker boots.
Panel 2 — Vark: 'You want me to write chemical fire.' Theo: 'Yes.' Let the absurdity sit in the mundane setting.

Panel 3 — 'There was no chemical fire.' / 'Then make one up.' Include an off-panel worker complaint about a missing boot only as environmental comedy, not as new dialogue lettering unless already scripted.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Establish the lower archives as materially older than the polished Spire: physical books, sealed records, dim controlled light. Rae arrives with the copied material and finds Adrian already there with a sealed volume.

Panel 2 — Medium two-shot across a narrow archive aisle. Rae stands beside an open cart of recovered papers; Adrian stands beside a sealed physical volume already removed from the shelf. Use 'You're in my archive.' / 'Not this part.' with both measuring the distance to the book and to each other.

Panel 3 — Rae says exactly, 'Redlin.' Adrian does not answer. Hold a silent reaction beat before continuing. Rae: 'You know what's on this.' Adrian: 'Enough to know you should destroy it.' Rae: 'That's convenient.' Adrian: 'Convenience has nothing to do with it.' Rae asks why the record was erased. Keep the sealed physical archive material in frame as evidence of deliberate concealment. Adrian: 'Because some histories were not lost.' Rae: 'What does that mean?' Adrian: 'They were removed.'

Panel 4 — Rae asks, 'By whom?' Adrian answers exactly, 'By people who remembered what happened when they stayed.' End on Rae looking from Adrian to the empty numbered shelf slot where the missing history should be, fingertips resting on the recovered volume.

dialogueInline.text: That's the part I'm not giving you.

summary: Theo races to hide the Marker before a patrol reaches Sector Four. Adrian watches until Theo's motive changes from proving the object exists to preventing others from possessing it, then quietly helps him conceal it.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Theo returns to Sector Four injured and clumsy, dragging spoil and wreckage over the exposed Marker before an approaching official patrol can arrive. Preserve the Marker geometry and excavation geography from S03.

Panel 2 — Adrian watches without helping. Theo: 'They're coming.' Adrian: 'Yes.' The countdown is visible through distant patrol lights or workers approaching, not an action-movie chase. Theo finally says, 'Help me.' Adrian challenges the change in motive: 'You spent years wanting proof.'

Panel 3 — Theo kneels in black spoil beside the partly exposed Marker, breathing hard, one injured hand pressed to the ground. 'I have it.' Adrian remains standing a few steps away. 'And now?' Theo looks toward the approaching patrol lights: 'Now I don't want them to have it.'
Panel 4 — Adrian: 'Good.' He immediately joins the concealment effort. Show ordinary physical work: spoil, scrap and collapsed material, not magical hiding.
Panel 5 — Patrol passes close enough to threaten discovery. Adrian uses calm envoy authority to redirect them toward the officially reported collapse.

Panel 6 — The Marker is fully hidden beneath rough black spoil and broken work debris. Theo and Adrian crouch in the foreground while the patrol lights recede down the wrong trench. Theo says, 'You could have helped five minutes ago.' Adrian answers, 'Five minutes ago you were still deciding what it belonged to.'

Panel 3 — 'You don't know that.' / 'Neither do you. That's the problem.' Their conflict is over authority without certainty.

Panel 5 — Rae feeds the copied record into an ordinary secure disposal slot and watches the last physical sheet disappear. Calum lunges one step too late, hand out toward the empty tray. Rae turns away from him and exits carrying nothing.

Adrian: 'You still think the location is the danger.' Theo: 'What is?' Adrian: 'Recognition.' Give the word space and keep the cutter present but clearly secondary to Theo's fear.
Panel 3 — Theo asks, 'What recognized me?' Adrian answers, 'That's the question.' Theo accuses him of knowing. Adrian: 'I know what it resembles.' Theo: 'What?'

Panel 4 — Final tight close on Adrian against the dark buried trench, the small preserved site record visible in his hand. He says only, 'A beginning.' Theo's industrial cutter remains low and out of focus in the foreground.

dialogueInline.text: The Marker reacted before you understood what you were looking at. I know what that means. I don't know why it happened to you.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Rae back inside the telemetry/archive system after destroying the copy, now severing the remaining identity trail that connects her to the recovered material. The room should look partially stripped of her institutional life.
Panel 2 — Adrian arrives after the damage: 'You burned it.' Rae: 'You told me to destroy the copy.'

Panel 3 — Adrian: 'I did.' Rae: 'I destroyed the trail.' Rae drops her archive badge and identification crystal onto the damaged desk beside the erased records; Adrian looks from the objects to her packed coat and bag.
Panel 4 — Adrian: 'That was your life.' Rae: 'No. It was my job.' Their difference in age and experience should be visible without paternalism.

Panel 5 — Adrian: 'The distinction matters now.' He breaks or disables the identification crystal the Spire could use to follow Rae. Rae: 'Where do I go?' Adrian: 'Somewhere you've never dreamed of.' Rae immediately catches the wording.

Panel 6 — Rae: 'How do you know about the dreams?' Adrian: 'Because you aren't the first.' End tight on Rae: her eyes widen slightly, then shift toward the sealed archive door as she grips the strap of her bag.

Panel 2 — Theo: 'You heard it too.' Adrian: 'Put the shard down.' Adrian has already stepped backward from the warming fragment, one hand braced against the wall. Theo watches that involuntary movement instead of the shard.

Panel 3 — Adrian: 'There are no canopies left to fracture.' Theo: 'But you remember them.' Final issue panel. Close on Adrian answering exactly: 'Yes.' Theo's relief that the impossible history is shared is immediately undercut by the realization that Adrian knows why.
